messages:
sienna (on-call): incident-bot just pushed a page: High 5xx spike on inference-serving across us-west-2. pagerduty-bot paged the on-call. Anyone seeing this on dashboards?
pagerduty-bot: Paging sienna (on-call) -> P1: inference-serving 5xx-rate > 8% (3m window)
incident-bot: Alert created: alert_id=INF-5XX-1834, rule=service:inference:5xx_rate. Context: recent deploy to dedicated pool.
alex: acked. i'm jumping in. first step: is this rollout still in progress or did it finish ~5m ago?
priya: rollout finished ~7m ago, can confirm by looking at deploy history. tag: release/optimize-kernel-2026
jamie: grabbing logs from the new pods now. running `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference --since=10m` to see errors.
oscar: dashboards — somethings odd: the 5xx spike corresponds to a small spike in median latency but huge increase in backend 429/503 from worker nodes. Possibly OOM/eviction or kernel mismatch.
maria: customer-impact check: we have 3 customers with elevated error rates, highest is partner-acme -> 22% failed requests in last 3m. CS alerted.
alex: running a quick canary split to route traffic away from the new pool: `redwood route set --service inference --exclude-pool kernel-opt-3` — doing now.
jamie: logs show repeated errors `CUDA kernel launch failed: invalid device function` on the new quantized kernels. stack snippet:
```
E 2026-06-07T09:58:12Z inference_worker kernel_runner.cpp:312 KernelLaunchError: invalid device function
  at kernel_runner.cc:312
  at engine_init.cc:87
```
oscar: that explains it — new kernel incompatible with older GPU microcode on some nodes. rolling back kernels should fix immediate 5xx.
priya: agree. rollback queued: `kubectl set image deployment/inference kernel-image=kernel-image:stable` and kick off a scale down of affected nodes. If rollback -> monitor for drop in 5xx.
sienna (on-call): good. alex, jamie, priya do rollback and confirm. i'll notify CS and run a quick customer impact assessment. ping me when traffic is stable.
alex: rollback applied to 4 deployments; I forced new pods on stable image. traffic routing removed from kernel-opt-3 pool.
jamie: pods restarted, I'm tailing logs. errors decreasing — 5xx rate dropped from 9% -> 1.2% over 2m.
maria: confirming with CS: partner-acme reports successful calls now. letting them know root cause is kernel incompatibility and we'll follow up.
priya: marking incident as mitigated. will keep monitoring for 15m. opening postmortem skeleton: `/docs/incidents/INF-5XX-1834` with initial notes.
oscar: two immediate action items after mitigation: (1) add node-level kernel compatibility check in deploy pipeline, (2) tune alerting to avoid pages for kernel-level transient failures that are only on small fraction of fleet.
alex: +1. also we should add a dashboard panel that correlates 5xx by pool and by kernel-image tag so we can triage faster next time.
incident-bot: Incident INF-5XX-1834 status: mitigated -> adding follow-up tasks to the incident ticket.
sienna (on-call): post-incident discussion point: our current alert rule triggers a P1 page whenever 5xx-rate > 8% for 3m regardless of topology. we need to refine so we don't page on rollout-related partial-fleet failures.
priya: proposed alerting changes (draft):
```
- severity: page
  condition: (global_5xx_rate >= 8% && total_rps >= 2000) || (pool_5xx_rate >= 12% && pool_rps >= 500)
  duration: 3m
- severity: ticket
  condition: (global_5xx_rate >= 5% && total_rps < 2000) || (pool_5xx_rate >= 8% && pool_rps < 500)
  duration: 10m
- suppression: deploy-tag-change windows -> suppress pages for 10m after deploys unless global_5xx_rate >= 15%
```
oscar: I like that. also add an exclusion for small customers so we don't page for noise from a single tiny partner — route to support first and only page when > X customers impacted.
maria: agree. add customer-impact dimension: page if number_of_customers_with_5xx >= 3 or any enterprise customer > 10% error.
alex: I'll create an Alertmanager route update: pages to eng-oncall channel for P1, tickets to eng-sre for P2. Adding explicit route for 'deploy-suppression' label to send to #eng-deployments instead of paging.
sienna (on-call): and we should avoid flapping: add a 2x refractory period in the alerting eval to prevent repeat pages within 30m for the same alert_id unless severity increases.
jamie: I'll draft the Prometheus rule and a grafana dashboard panel. snippet for the rule (rough):
```
alert: InferenceHigh5xxByPool
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5..",pool!~"dev"}[3m])) by (pool) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{pool}[3m])) by (pool) > 0.12
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/inference-5xx
```
priya: assign followups: @alex update alertmanager routes, @jamie add dashboard + rule PR, @oscar add deploy pipeline kernel compatibility check, @maria coordinate customer comms and postmortem entry. I'll own the postmortem skeleton.
sienna (on-call): handoff note for next on-call: mitigation done, monitoring watch for 30m. please escalate to me if 5xx > 5% persists or if new customers report failures. I'll be reachable for 2 hours.
alex: PRs opened: `infra/alerts#314` (alert tweaks) and `dashboards/inference#22` (pool tag panels). please review.
maria: filed incident ticket INF-5XX-1834 with customer-impact blurb and assigned to postmortem. CS notified partners with ETA for root cause analysis.
jamie: quick retrospective: runbook was helpful, but we need a checklist item to check kernel-image tags vs node microcode versions before rollout. adding to runbook.
oscar: longterm: consider routing policy change: only page when an anomaly crosses multiple pools OR impacts > N customers — otherwise create severity=ticket and route to eng-sre with an on-call assignment window.
sienna (on-call): thanks team. closing the mitigation phase. leaving thread open for the tuning work and PR reviews. will update when postmortem is ready. :white_check_mark:
